note: Multimodal is deliberately excluded from the composite and shown as a separate vision score, so that text-only models are never ranked against a category they do not compete in.
min_coverage_rationale: Renormalising over available weight lets a thinly measured model rank high on what it is missing rather than on being better. Models below the bar are shown in a provisional section instead of competing for a top-N slot. The bar is 4 of 5 so that a new model with all four benchmarks but no Arena votes yet still ranks, flagged as awaiting human votes.
min_release_date_rationale: This is a frontier-model scoreboard, not a historical archive of every model Epoch has ever measured - Epoch's own registry goes back years further than this. The cutoff keeps the catalogue to models a reader would recognise as current. It is arbitrary in the way any cutoff is: a model released the day before it is invisible to the whole site, never even shown as provisional. Debatable by PR like every other number here.

normalization.lmarena: min-max normalized across the cohort present in each build

rules: Only human_eval and third_party_benchmark feed the composite.
vendor_claim values are stored and displayed, never scored.
Models missing a category are scored on available weight and marked partial.
Models below min_coverage_for_ranking are provisional, never ranked.
SWE-bench scaffold results never count as a bare-model score.

equating.method: mean-sigma linear equating onto the category anchor
equating.anchors_rationale: The anchor sets each category's level and spread, so it is fixed here rather than chosen by count each build: by count, GPQA (near its ceiling) and OTIS overtook LiveBench on 2026-10-01 and would have compressed Reasoning and moved every score with no model changing. LiveBench is the contamination-resistant, mid-range scale the categories already used.
equating.min_correlation_test: one-sided t-test of the paired correlation at 5%
equating.gate_rationale: Equating assumes both benchmarks measure the same thing. A benchmark whose correlation with the anchor is not significantly positive on the shared models is shown but not scored; the test scales with the overlap, so 6 shared models need r > 0.73 while 50 need r > 0.24. On 2026-10-01 this leaves SWE-bench Verified unscored (r = 0.14 over 6 shared models).

display_only.frontiermath: Superseded by FrontierMath Tiers 1-3 v2 in Epoch's benchmark metadata. Shown, and still counts as a source, but scoring both would count one benchmark family twice.

equating.rationale: Benchmarks inside one category sit at very different levels (FrontierMath averaged 31.9 against LiveBench Math's 89.5 on 2026-09-29), so a plain mean scored models on which benchmark they were given. Equating on models measured on both cut the leave-one-out substitution drift from 31.52 to 3.55 points for SimpleQA and from 19.17 to 2.37 for FrontierMath v2.
